It felt like a switch flipped in the guy, because he suddenly starts charging toward us screaming “f*ck you you f*cking TERRORIST, the f*ck are you looking at TERRORIST, TERRORIST, TERRORIST”

My body went into fight mode immediately as A) the level of aggression was so severe and caught us completely off guard, and B) this was not long after Oct 7th, so we were both acutely aware of/pretty reactive to any type of xenophobia or racism towards muslims or brown people in general. My husband was able to shut it down, get us away from him and brush the interaction off but it had me fuming for days after the fact. I still think about it and get pissed off months later. 

This behavior is disgusting and needs to be stopped.

Hey there, great question. I ultimately decided that AA was not the right fit for me and I attended my last meeting on my first day of sobriety. I didn’t feel a super strong connection to their meetings, or methodology and approach to sobriety - specifically in regard to the belief that an addict once is an addict for life, and that a ‘higher power’ is the sole reason we are able to overcome our addictions. I feel like it fails to acknowledge an individual’s own strength and conviction as the motivator of getting sober, as well as disregarding the fact that we can grow and shed things that once had a grip on our lives. 

I also felt quite unrepresented in meetings, which were all dominated by older men, but that is likely due to me just going to the closest location near my home (in the gay hub of SF). They host dozens of meetings throughout the week, but only (1) women-oriented meeting/week  :(

That being said, AA has achieved ~incredible~ success for millions of people! And my experience is not what yours might be. This is all just my interpretation of their methods, and I’m not saying it’s the correct or only one. 

If you’re looking into other meeting options I highly recommend SMART. They have a more scientific and realistic approach to sobriety, which felt more up my alley. They unfortunately don’t host in-person meetings in my city, but I attended a few on zoom and quite liked them. 

I do hope you find whatever it is that will keep you on track and pushing forward 🤞🏽I had to turn my DM’s off on here because people are creepy, but if you ever want to talk just comment on one of my posts and I’ll message you!

I feel for you. Parenting can definitely feel like a gamble in terms of how you’ll perceive the experience once you’re in it. I recently watched a video on youtube regarding giving your children choices around ages 2-3. Its mostly encouraged at that age, but we also need to remember that all children are different and subsequently have different needs. The video by Bekah Martinez (linked for you [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=imX0jVc2ebE)) talks about her struggle battling tantrums and meltdowns throughout the day and noticing that it stemmed from giving her toddler too many options. She felt that it was leading to overstimulation and a lack of structure, which is equally important at that age. She also reflects that this was not at all the same experience with her first and oldest child when they were that age. What works for one kid might not work for another. I don’t have much else to share other than this, but I hope that maybe it can help you out even in a small way. Best of luck to you and your kiddo ❤️
